correctness.rationale: Obstruction for >=3 whites on either shore is invariant, equal two-by-two white pairs have no initial force, distinct two-by-two pairs are forced by explicit 4-step sequences, and monotonicity handles all smaller profiles. The binomial profile count and discriminant analysis are algebraic consequences. Independent forcing-process verifier exhaustively checks all 349504 subsets for n=3..9; infinite statement is proved, not extrapolated from those checks.

evidence: Boyer et al. Proposition 4 counts K_{a_1,...,a_k}; nonadjacency in crowns is not a multipartite equivalence relation. Proposition 6 covers the C_6 special case. Brimkov–Carlson general minimal-set results do not determine all crown profiles. Grood et al. characterize trees, crowns are non-trees. Jacob proves a general span relation without evaluating it for crowns.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results cover definitions, general extremal coefficients, special n=3, or other graph classes. They do not logically determine the full polynomial for every n>=4 without an additional structural classification.

evidence: 2018 formula for complete multipartite graphs has only three possible nonzero degrees, but crown formula has five for n>=3; crowns are not multipartite. The span identity is tautological once Z and F are known and cannot imply the count c(c-1). The 2022 failed-forcing product paper omits categorical products and considers maximal failed sets. The minimal-set and well-forced papers focus on different generalities and graph families.
